sentences.text: Chacaicosaurus is an extinct genus of long-snouted thunnosaurian ichthyosaur classified within the superorder Ichthyopterygia, order Ichthyosauria, suborder Neoichthyosauria, and infraorder Thunnosauria.
The holotype skull of Chacaicosaurus measures 98 cm in length, while its lower jaw extends to 99 cm.
The snout features elongate, rounded ridges running along the premaxillae and nasals on each side.
The external nostrils of this animal measure approximately 10 cm in length.
Its forelimbs contain four main digits, with the longest digit holding at least 14 bone elements, and an accessory digit situated behind the primary digits that ends before the wrist.
Adult Chacaicosaurus likely possessed very reduced teeth or was entirely toothless.
Chacaicosaurus and Mollesaurus are the only diagnostic ichthyosaur specimens known from the interval between the Aalenian and Bathonian stages.
Based on skull size, Chacaicosaurus appears significantly larger than the genus Stenopterygius.
The genus Chacaicosaurus was named by Marta S. Fernández in 1994 for the species Chacaicosaurus cayi.
The only known specimen was discovered in northwestern Patagonia, Argentina, near the city of Zapala in the Neuquén Basin.
This fossil was found in the Los Molles Formation of Neuquén Province.
Strong incisions on the forelimb and a rounded humerus in the holotype suggest the specimen represents an adult.
Jurassic ichthyosaurs like Chacaicosaurus swam using carangiform or thunniform propulsion, moving their tails side-to-side like modern tuna.
Chacaicosaurus was likely a fast swimmer that hunted by chasing prey visually using its large eyes.
Ichthyosaurs like Chacaicosaurus had high metabolisms and could regulate their body temperatures.
Ichthyosaurs gave birth to live young underwater rather than laying eggs.
Chacaicosaurus lived in open marine waters sharing its habitat with Mollesaurus, plesiosaurs, thalattosuchians, and invertebrates.
Recent cladistic analyses place Chacaicosaurus as a basal thunnosaurian outside both Stenopterygiidae and Ophthalmosauridae.
Some analyses identify Chacaicosaurus as the sister taxon to Ophthalmosauridae, with Stenopterygius being the closest relative to that group.
Classification of Chacaicosaurus is debated, with some authors placing it in Thunnosauria near ophthalmosaurids and others placing it outside Thunnosauria near Hauffiopteryx.
Some researchers classify Chacaicosaurus within the genus Stenopterygius as S. cayi, a suggestion originally made by Fernández in 2007.
Researchers Erin Maxwell and colleagues argued in 2012 that Chacaicosaurus should be considered a synonym of Stenopterygius due to shared traits.
Chacaicosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, specifically the early Bajocian stage, approximately 171.6 to 170 million years ago.
Fossil records place Chacaicosaurus in the Bajocian stage between 170.9 and 168.6 million years ago.
The geological zone containing Chacaicosaurus dates to the early Bajocian, spanning roughly 170.3 to 168.3 million years ago.
The environment where Chacaicosaurus lived was an open ocean with lowering sea levels.
Pollen evidence suggests the climate near Chacaicosaurus' habitat was warm with alternating damp and dry conditions.
There is a scientific debate regarding the size of the orbits in Chacaicosaurus, with some researchers suggesting they were small and others claiming they were large.
It is debated whether Chacaicosaurus is more closely related to Ophthalmosauridae or other thunnosaurians, as different phylogenetic analyses yield conflicting results.
